newsitem.title: UK: BA takes off on fresh American hopes.
newsitem.headline: BA takes off on fresh American hopes.

text.p: Shares in British Airways jumped 8.0 pence to 562.5 pence by 0935 GMT on Wednesday amid renewed optimism that any the airline's proposed alliance with American Airlines will be shown a green light, analysts said.

Analysts said that although they expected British Trade and Industry Minister Ian Lang to impose conditions on any approval of the controversial deal, which has roused fierce opposition from rival airlines, these may not derail the proposed alliance.
"The whole thing is looking much more workable," said Peter Bergius, airlines analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. "The mood of optimism (in the market) is improving all the time."
The industry has been braced for Lang's ruling since he received the results on September 17 of a three-month investigation into the planned alliance by his Office of Fair Trading (OFT).
Any clearance of the deal by Lang is expected to hinge on opening up to competition BA's home hub of London Heathrow.

Analyst are expecting Lang's decision on whether to block or approve the deal next month -- coinciding with the resumption of talks between the UK and U.S. on an "open skies" agreement across the Atlantic.
As British authorities confirmed that open skies trade talks, that broke down three months ago, were due to resume in Washington on November 6, BA's shares strengthened further.
By 0950 GMT, they were trading 12p higher at 566.5 pence.
